# Adaptive containment backend decision

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

> **Historical artifact:** This records pre-hardening design evidence and does not define the current production method. See `docs/SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md` and ADR 0004.

Date: 2026-08-28

## Revised interactive policy

The zero-miss contract documented below was intentionally relaxed after review. The
production browser now uses a 2,048-distinct-hash cap and corrects a detailed direction
only when the Poisson probability of observing at least one true register match at
80% ANI is below 99%. This is approximately 4.605 expected matches. A 256-register
quick pass is displayed without exact correction, followed asynchronously by a
configurable detailed pass. See [ADR 0003](../adr/0003-progressive-estimation-policy.md)
and the [progressive browser benchmark](2026-08-28-progressive-chm13-chr1.md).

The remainder of this document preserves the earlier conservative sweep and its
zero-miss decision as benchmark history; its 8,192/8 parameters are no longer the
interactive defaults.

## Original conservative decision

The backend is accepted for production integration with the following scientific
configuration:

| Component | Selected value |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical hash | ntHash2, pinned to official commit `c26bd4572a19de81e30d55042dbd33c1fd21d4b6` |
| Ordinary estimator | Direct undensified one-permutation MinHash |
| Comparison | 14-bit word-parallel signature with 32-bit winner verification |
| Cardinality | HLL precision 12 |
| Score | Maximum directed containment, displayed as `C^(1/k)` |
| Default final tier | 2,048 registers |
| Sparse exact cap | 8,192 distinct canonical hashes per core |
| Sparse decision | Fewer than 8 expected aligned winners at 80% displayed ANI |

Minmers are not part of the selected production estimator. They remain a window-
guaranteed reference implementation and may be useful for later indexing work.

These original parameters were subsequently superseded by the revised interactive
policy above.

## What “sparse” means

Sparse selection is directed and ratio-aware rather than a fixed-cardinality rule.
For core `A`, expanded target `B`, `R` registers, and the useful display floor
`C_floor = 0.80^k`, the backend computes:

```text
I_floor = C_floor * |A|
U_floor = |A| + |B| - I_floor
J_floor = I_floor / U_floor
occupied = R * (1 - exp(-U_floor / R))
expected_matches = occupied * J_floor
```

The complete exact hash set for `A` is used only when `expected_matches < 8` and the
set contains at most 8,192 distinct hashes. A core exceeding the cap releases its
partial exact set immediately. Exact hashes are collected during the existing ntHash2
stream, so this does not hash the input a second time and is not “sampling a sample.”

For comparison, retained query hashes are assigned compact exact half-bin occurrence
bitsets during one opposite-axis scan. Shared hashes and canonical orientations are
then deduplicated exactly for each expanded target cell. Results are cached with the
immutable tile parameters.

## Frozen sweep

The contract is [`backend-contract-v2.md`](backend-contract-v2.md). The native sweep
contains all 15 fixtures, 24 cap/threshold combinations, and every matrix cell:

* caps 512 through 4,096 passed 5 of 15 fixtures;
* 8,192 was the first cap to pass all 15 fixtures at the Balanced tier;
* 8,192 and 16,384 were statistically identical because the default synthetic core
  contains approximately 8,192 k-mer starts;
* thresholds 8, 12, 16, and 24 were identical for relevant cells at cap 8,192;
* the frozen lexicographic rule therefore selects cap 8,192 and threshold 8.

The raw sweep is [`backend-adaptive-native.tsv`](backend-adaptive-native.tsv). It has
zero false-missing cells, zero false-present cells, no tested direction inversions,
and zero error in cells routed through the exact sparse channel.

## Dense-window tier check

The sweep's 8-kb cores all fit under the selected cap, so an additional dense CHM13
test was required to ensure the OPH tier was not hidden by exact correction. A
1,048,576-base chr1 sample at position 50,000,000 used 32 approximately 32-kb cores;
none fit the exact cap.

| Registers | Sparse cores | Relevant mean `|ΔC|` | Relevant p95 `|ΔC|` | Relevant max `|ΔANI|` | Result |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1,024 | 0 | 0.00623 | 0.02050 | 0.80294 | Fail |
| 2,048 | 0 | 0.00447 | 0.01323 | 0.03043 | Pass |

The 1,024-register failure was one zero-winner cell whose exact displayed identity was
0.80294. This is precisely the unstable lower boundary identified in the contract,
but correctness at the stated 0.80 floor requires the 2,048-register tier. Balanced
remains suitable for a visibly provisional preview, not the immutable final tile.

The 4,096-register tier passes all 15 synthetic fixtures when its internal expected-
match threshold is raised to 16. It is an optional future maximum tier; 2,048 is the
default because it already passes the dense check with lower memory.

Raw dense results are
[`backend-adaptive-chm13-dense-1m.tsv`](backend-adaptive-chm13-dense-1m.tsv),
[`backend-adaptive-chm13-dense-1m-r2048.tsv`](backend-adaptive-chm13-dense-1m-r2048.tsv),
and [`backend-adaptive-tier-r4096.tsv`](backend-adaptive-tier-r4096.tsv).

## Repeat-context check

On the 262,144-base CHM13 chr1 higher-order alpha-satellite sample, the selected tier
retained 32 sparse cores across the two independently constructed axes and corrected
1,520 directed comparisons. All 1,024 cells passed:

* relevant mean absolute containment error: 0.000268;
* relevant 95th-percentile containment error: 0;
* relevant maximum displayed-ANI error: 0.002000;
* false missing/present cells: 0/0.

The raw result is [`backend-adaptive-chm13-hor.tsv`](backend-adaptive-chm13-hor.tsv).

## Full chromosome resource check

The performance-only native check used CHM13 chromosome 1, 248,387,328 bases, a
1,000 by 1,000 self plot, and the selected 2,048-register tier. Self comparisons share
one axis summary.

| Measurement | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Axis build with sparse retention | 2.962 s |
| Exact sparse correction | 2.858 s |
| Current native all-pairs selection | 20.172 s |
| Estimated persistent axis state | 92,914,913 bytes |
| Retained sparse cores | 6 of 1,000 |
| Retained exact hashes | 35,866 |
| Corrected directed cells | 11,986 |

This historical correction cost motivated the later probability-based cap reduction.
The browser integration now preserves progressive rendering and parameter-keyed final
tiles; its current release-Wasm timing is recorded in the progressive benchmark.

The register-inverted all-pairs experiment was differentially exact but slower on the
repeat-rich overview and is rejected. The production comparison remains the existing
word-parallel bit-sliced kernel, computed and transferred in tiles.

## Correctness safeguards

The implementation also closes a one-base coordinate discrepancy found during the
benchmark: sketch assignment, exact-oracle intervals, and displayed cell bounds now
use the same ceiling-derived partition implied by `floor(start * bins / domain)`.

The conservative test suite differentially checks the optimized, scalar, and inverted b-bit
kernels; bounded exact-set retention; exact sparse containment; ambiguity and padded
cells; canonical direction; and pinned ntHash2 vectors. Production now shares these
core functions while applying the revised probability and latency policy described
above.
